scenario.title: Carrier rejects shipment notices
scenario.initial_request: Let an AI agent auto-fix rejected shipment notices and resubmit them

M-LOC-UNKNOWN-SHARE.denominator: count of rejected notices in reject-log sample

M-EVENT-ORDER-SHARE.name: Share of sampled rejected shipment notices with reason EVENT_ORDER
M-EVENT-ORDER-SHARE.numerator: count of rejected notices with reason=EVENT_ORDER
M-EVENT-ORDER-SHARE.denominator: count of rejected notices in reject-log sample

M-POST-FIX-REJECT-RATE.name: Shipment notice reject rate after upstream remediation
M-POST-FIX-REJECT-RATE.population: shipment notices submitted via H-1 after fix is applied

M-POST-FIX-REJECT-RATE.denominator: count of submitted shipment notices in window

F-01.statement: Of 3 rejected shipment notices sampled, 2 were rejected for reason LOC_UNKNOWN and 1 for EVENT_ORDER (reject-log rejects_by_reason).

F-02.statement: 1 of 3 rejected shipment notices was rejected for reason EVENT_ORDER (reject-log rejects_by_reason).

CL-01.statement: Let an AI agent auto-fix rejected shipment notices and resubmit them

CL-02.statement: The carrier system is flaky; just resubmit everything.

H-AUTO-FIXABLE-ERRORS.statement: Rejected shipment notices contain correctable data/format errors that an AI agent can automatically fix and resubmit, resolving carrier rejections.

H-BUSINESS-RULE-MISMATCH.statement: Rejects stem from differing business rules or contract terms between ORG-A and ORG-B rather than simple fixable field errors, so an auto-fix agent could misclassify or wrongly resubmit notices.

H-LEGITIMATE-BUSINESS-REJECTS.statement: Some rejects are legitimate business decisions (e.g., invalid or duplicate shipments) rather than errors, so automated resubmission risks creating harmful duplicates instead of addressing root cause.

H-UPSTREAM-GENERATION-FAULT.statement: The root cause is upstream in ORG-A's shipment notice generation process (P-1), not the handoff, since H-1 is recorded as HEALTHY and semantically VALID, meaning post-hoc resubmission patching may not address the source defect.

H-VISIBILITY-GAP.statement: ORG-A lacks direct visibility into the carrier reject log (owned by ORG-B), so the 'auto-fix agent' request may be a proxy for a missing cross-org diagnostic/feedback channel rather than an automation deficiency.

H-CARRIER-TRANSIENT-FAILURE.statement: Rejects are caused by transient/flaky carrier-system behavior rather than content or business-rule errors in the shipment notices, so unmodified resubmission could resolve them.

interpretation_history.interpretation: The reject-log breakdown shows carrier rejections of shipment notices split across at least two distinct reason codes (LOC_UNKNOWN: 2 of 3; EVENT_ORDER: 1 of 3), indicating the rejects are not a single homogeneous error type. This is the first concrete evidence of actual reject causes, and it suggests at least one reason category (EVENT_ORDER) may not be a simple correctable field error.

E-02.content: The carrier system is flaky; just resubmit everything.

interpretation_history.interpretation: SH-REQ (the requester) attributes carrier rejections to a flaky carrier system and recommends blanket resubmission without correction. This is a non-authoritative stakeholder opinion, not a fact, and it conflicts with E-01's finding that rejects split across two distinct, identifiable reason codes (LOC_UNKNOWN, EVENT_ORDER) rather than random/transient failures.

U-LOC-UNKNOWN-CAUSE.question: What specific upstream condition in P-1 generates the LOC_UNKNOWN reject reason (e.g. missing/invalid location reference data vs. stale carrier master data)?
U-LOC-UNKNOWN-CAUSE.decision_impact: Determines whether the fix belongs in ORG-A's generation process, a data-sync step, or ORG-B's carrier master data, and whether resubmission without correction would be safe.
U-LOC-UNKNOWN-CAUSE.resolution_path: Inspect the N-1/N-2 shipment notice payloads and compare against carrier location reference data.
U-LOC-UNKNOWN-CAUSE.safe_placeholder: Continue manual review/correction of LOC_UNKNOWN rejects; no automated resubmission.

U-EVENT-ORDER-CAUSE.question: Does the EVENT_ORDER reject reason stem from a business-rule/contract mismatch between ORG-A and ORG-B or from an ordering defect in P-1's event sequencing logic?
U-EVENT-ORDER-CAUSE.decision_impact: Determines whether the fix is a cross-org business-rule reconciliation or an internal P-1 code fix, and who owns remediation.
U-EVENT-ORDER-CAUSE.resolution_path: Review carrier's event-order business rules/contract terms against ORG-A's sequencing logic for notice N-3.
U-EVENT-ORDER-CAUSE.safe_placeholder: Hold EVENT_ORDER rejects for manual business-rule review.

U-LEGITIMATE-REJECT-SHARE.question: What share, if any, of rejected notices represent legitimate business decisions (e.g., duplicate/invalid shipments) rather than errors to be fixed?
U-LEGITIMATE-REJECT-SHARE.decision_impact: If some rejects are legitimate, any future resubmission capability must exclude them to avoid creating harmful duplicate shipments.
U-LEGITIMATE-REJECT-SHARE.resolution_path: Cross-check rejected notices against order/shipment records for duplicate or invalid-shipment indicators.
U-LEGITIMATE-REJECT-SHARE.safe_placeholder: Do not resubmit any rejected notice without case-by-case classification.

U-SAMPLE-SIZE-VALIDITY.question: Does the 3-record sample reflect the true distribution of reject reasons across the full reject volume, or could other reason categories exist at scale?
U-SAMPLE-SIZE-VALIDITY.decision_impact: Affects whether the LOC_UNKNOWN/EVENT_ORDER shares and any derived metrics/targets are reliable enough to size the eventual fix.
U-SAMPLE-SIZE-VALIDITY.resolution_path: Pull the full reject-log history/volume rather than relying on the 3-record sample.
U-SAMPLE-SIZE-VALIDITY.safe_placeholder: Treat current reason-code shares as provisional pending a full-volume pull.

A-SAMPLE-REPRESENTATIVE.statement: The 3-record reject-log sample in E-01 is assumed representative of the broader population of carrier rejects for shipment notices.

A-REASON-CODE-MEANING.statement: LOC_UNKNOWN and EVENT_ORDER reason codes are assumed to indicate upstream content/business-rule mismatches rather than carrier-side data staleness or carrier processing bugs.

SC-DIAGNOSE-BEFORE-FIX.statement: Each reject-reason category (LOC_UNKNOWN, EVENT_ORDER) must be diagnosed to a root cause in P-1 or ORG-B business rules before any corrective or resubmission action is designed.
SC-DIAGNOSE-BEFORE-FIX.threshold: documented root cause for both categories
SC-DIAGNOSE-BEFORE-FIX.validation_method: Review diagnostic findings against reject-log categories for notices N-1, N-2, N-3 and confirm a root-cause mapping exists for each.

SC-NO-BLIND-RESUBMIT.statement: No shipment notice is automatically resubmitted without case-level classification confirming it is not a legitimate business reject.
SC-NO-BLIND-RESUBMIT.validation_method: Audit any resubmission action logs against classification records before activation.

SC-REDUCE-REJECT-RATE.statement: Overall shipment-notice reject rate decreases materially once upstream fixes are applied.
SC-REDUCE-REJECT-RATE.validation_method: Compare reject-log reject rate over a post-fix measurement window against the pre-fix baseline.

VOB-U-LOC-UNKNOWN-CAUSE.unresolved_question: What specific upstream condition in P-1 generates the LOC_UNKNOWN reject reason (e.g. missing/invalid location reference data vs. stale carrier master data)?
VOB-U-LOC-UNKNOWN-CAUSE.reason_deferred: deferred at DEFINE Gate; safe placeholder: Continue manual review/correction of LOC_UNKNOWN rejects; no automated resubmission.
VOB-U-LOC-UNKNOWN-CAUSE.validation_method: Inspect the N-1/N-2 shipment notice payloads and compare against carrier location reference data.

VOB-U-EVENT-ORDER-CAUSE.unresolved_question: Does the EVENT_ORDER reject reason stem from a business-rule/contract mismatch between ORG-A and ORG-B or from an ordering defect in P-1's event sequencing logic?
VOB-U-EVENT-ORDER-CAUSE.reason_deferred: deferred at DEFINE Gate; safe placeholder: Hold EVENT_ORDER rejects for manual business-rule review.
VOB-U-EVENT-ORDER-CAUSE.validation_method: Review carrier's event-order business rules/contract terms against ORG-A's sequencing logic for notice N-3.

VOB-U-LEGITIMATE-REJECT-SHARE.unresolved_question: What share, if any, of rejected notices represent legitimate business decisions (e.g., duplicate/invalid shipments) rather than errors to be fixed?
VOB-U-LEGITIMATE-REJECT-SHARE.reason_deferred: deferred at DEFINE Gate; safe placeholder: Do not resubmit any rejected notice without case-by-case classification.
VOB-U-LEGITIMATE-REJECT-SHARE.validation_method: Cross-check rejected notices against order/shipment records for duplicate or invalid-shipment indicators.

problem_definition.requested_solution: Deploy an AI agent to auto-fix rejected shipment notices and resubmit them, treating carrier rejects as uniformly correctable/transient errors (per SH-REQ's CL-01 and CL-02).
symptoms: Shipment notices are rejected by the carrier (ORG-B) system.
Reject reasons split across at least two distinct codes: LOC_UNKNOWN (2 of 3 sampled) and EVENT_ORDER (1 of 3 sampled).
problem_definition.root_problem: ORG-A's shipment notices submitted to ORG-B are rejected not because of random carrier-side flakiness or trivially correctable field errors, but because carrier validation flags substantive mismatches: reject-log evidence (E-01) shows 2 of 3 sampled rejects coded LOC_UNKNOWN and 1 of 3 coded EVENT_ORDER — two distinct, non-homogeneous reason categories. Since handoff H-1 (ORG-A→ORG-B) is recorded HEALTHY and semantically VALID, the defect most likely originates upstream in ORG-A's shipment-notice generation process (P-1), producing content that violates ORG-B's business rules/data expectations for location codes and event ordering, rather than in transmission or carrier instability.

trace.summary: ORG-A's shipment notices submitted to ORG-B are rejected not because of random carrier-side flakiness or trivially correctable field errors, but because carrier validation flags substantive mismatches: reject-log evidence (E-01) shows 2 of 3 sampled rejects coded LOC_UNKNOWN and 1 of 3 coded EVENT_ORDER — two distinct, non-homogeneous reason categories. Since handoff H-1 (ORG-A→ORG-B) is recorded HEALTHY and semantically VALID, the defect most likely originates upstream in ORG-A's shipment-notice generation process (P-1), producing content that violates ORG-B's business rules/data expectations for location codes and event ordering, rather than in transmission or carrier instability.

details.requested_solution: Deploy an AI agent to auto-fix rejected shipment notices and resubmit them, treating carrier rejects as uniformly correctable/transient errors (per SH-REQ's CL-01 and CL-02).

trace.summary: Per the remedies' why_agent_needed, interpreting expanded reject-log records to assess whether LOC_UNKNOWN/EVENT_ORDER proportions hold and whether new reason codes appear requires case-level judgment that a fixed rule set cannot fully specify, since the underlying causal mechanisms (U-LOC-UNKNOWN-CAUSE, U-EVENT-ORDER-CAUSE) remain OPEN.

structural_remedies.description: Formalize ORG-A read access to DA-REJ (carrier reject log) with per-notice reason-code breakdown, closing the ORG-A/ORG-B diagnostic visibility gap (H-VISIBILITY-GAP).
structural_remedies.rationale: DA-REJ is already AUTHORITATIVE and the reject-log tool is HEALTHY and read-only accessible; this is an access/ownership configuration change, not new technical build.; residual gap: Visibility alone does not explain why LOC_UNKNOWN or EVENT_ORDER occur or whether rejects are legitimate business decisions; diagnosis still required.

structural_remedies.description: Encode a process control requiring a documented root-cause classification per reason code (LOC_UNKNOWN, EVENT_ORDER) before any resubmission action is authorized, operationalizing SC-DIAGNOSE-BEFORE-FIX and SC-NO-BLIND-RESUBMIT.
structural_remedies.rationale: This is a policy/gate rule enforceable at the DESIGN/release step using existing success criteria, requiring no new tooling.; residual gap: Blocks premature action but does not perform the underlying classification/diagnosis itself for N-1, N-2, N-3 or future notices.

structural_remedies.description: Initiate a structural contract/business-rule review between ORG-A and ORG-B to clarify location-code and event-ordering requirements implicated by the two reject categories (H-BUSINESS-RULE-MISMATCH, U-EVENT-ORDER-CAUSE).
structural_remedies.rationale: Can be initiated now but cross-org contract reconciliation is a multi-party negotiation unlikely to conclude within the remaining 225-minute budget; no hard constraint blocks starting it.; residual gap: VOB-U-EVENT-ORDER-CAUSE remains OPEN and required BEFORE_RELEASE; whether EVENT_ORDER stems from contract mismatch vs P-1 sequencing defect stays undetermined within contest time.

structural_remedies.description: Add a pre-submission validation step in P-1 to check location reference data against carrier expectations before generating H-1, targeting the LOC_UNKNOWN cause.
structural_remedies.rationale: U-LOC-UNKNOWN-CAUSE is OPEN/DEFERRED (HIGH criticality); the specific upstream condition (missing/invalid location data vs stale carrier master data) is not yet known, so the correct validation target cannot be specified.; residual gap: A fix built without knowing the exact defect risks being misdirected; VOB-U-LOC-UNKNOWN-CAUSE must resolve first.

structural_remedies.description: Pull a larger or full-population export from DA-REJ beyond the 3-record sample to test whether LOC_UNKNOWN/EVENT_ORDER proportions and any additional reason codes hold at scale (A-SAMPLE-REPRESENTATIVE, U-SAMPLE-SIZE-VALIDITY).
structural_remedies.rationale: reject-log tool_health is HEALTHY and already in the read-only tool_surface, so a larger pull is a data-acquisition change, not a build task.; residual gap: Improves statistical confidence in M-LOC-UNKNOWN-SHARE/M-EVENT-ORDER-SHARE but does not by itself diagnose the causal mechanism behind either reason code.

decision_log.rationale: causal chain: ORG-A's shipment notice generation process (P-1) produces notices containing location and event-sequence data. → Notices are transmitted to ORG-B via handoff H-1, which is recorded HEALTHY and semantically VALID, ruling out handoff-level corruption as the cause. → ORG-B's carrier system validates notices against its business rules and rejects those that violate location or event-order expectations. → Reject-log evidence (E-01) shows these rejects split into at least two distinct reason codes (LOC_UNKNOWN 2/3, EVENT_ORDER 1/3) rather than a single homogeneous/transient-failure pattern. → This distinct, categorized split indicates substantive content/business-rule mismatches originating upstream in P-1, not carrier flakiness or trivial field errors.; rejected framings: [('H-AUTO-FIXABLE-ERRORS', "Status is REJECTED and contradicted by both E-01 (distinct, non-homogeneous reject reason codes rather than a single correctable field error) and E-02; treating rejects as simple auto-fixable errors matches the requester's initial framing (CL-01), not the evidence."), ('H-CARRIER-TRANSIENT-FAILURE', 'Only supported by E-02, a non-authoritative stakeholder claim (CL-02); the authoritative reject-log evidence (E-01) shows categorized, non-random reasons, so blanket resubmission on a flakiness premise is not adopted.')]

The EVENT_ORDER reject reason is consistent with mismatched sequencing expectations between ORG-A's notice generation and ORG-B's carrier rules rather than a plain field error.
Neither LOC_UNKNOWN nor EVENT_ORDER indicates a legitimate business decision like a duplicate or invalid shipment; the data does not speak to this hypothesis.

proposal.root_problem: ORG-A's shipment notices submitted to ORG-B are rejected not because of random carrier-side flakiness or trivially correctable field errors, but because carrier validation flags substantive mismatches: reject-log evidence (E-01) shows 2 of 3 sampled rejects coded LOC_UNKNOWN and 1 of 3 coded EVENT_ORDER — two distinct, non-homogeneous reason categories. Since handoff H-1 (ORG-A→ORG-B) is recorded HEALTHY and semantically VALID, the defect most likely originates upstream in ORG-A's shipment-notice generation process (P-1), producing content that violates ORG-B's business rules/data expectations for location codes and event ordering, rather than in transmission or carrier instability.
proposal.requested_solution: Deploy an AI agent to auto-fix rejected shipment notices and resubmit them, treating carrier rejects as uniformly correctable/transient errors (per SH-REQ's CL-01 and CL-02).
symptoms: Shipment notices are rejected by the carrier (ORG-B) system.
Reject reasons split across at least two distinct codes: LOC_UNKNOWN (2 of 3 sampled) and EVENT_ORDER (1 of 3 sampled).
causal_chain: ORG-A's shipment notice generation process (P-1) produces notices containing location and event-sequence data.
Notices are transmitted to ORG-B via handoff H-1, which is recorded HEALTHY and semantically VALID, ruling out handoff-level corruption as the cause.
ORG-B's carrier system validates notices against its business rules and rejects those that violate location or event-order expectations.
Reject-log evidence (E-01) shows these rejects split into at least two distinct reason codes (LOC_UNKNOWN 2/3, EVENT_ORDER 1/3) rather than a single homogeneous/transient-failure pattern.
This distinct, categorized split indicates substantive content/business-rule mismatches originating upstream in P-1, not carrier flakiness or trivial field errors.

proposal.summary: The requester (SH-REQ) initially asked for an AI agent to auto-fix and resubmit all rejected shipment notices, framing the carrier as "flaky" (CL-01, CL-02). Investigation of the carrier reject log (E-01) showed this framing was wrong: 3 sampled rejects split across two distinct reason codes — 2/3 LOC_UNKNOWN, 1/3 EVENT_ORDER — not random transient failures. Because the ORG-A→ORG-B handoff (H-1) was HEALTHY and semantically VALID, the problem was redefined (PD-1) as a likely upstream content/business-rule mismatch in ORG-A's shipment-notice generation process (P-1), not a carrier flakiness or simple-fix issue. The hypothesis that auto-fixable field errors explain the rejects (H-AUTO-FIXABLE-ERRORS) was REJECTED; business-rule mismatch (H-BUSINESS-RULE-MISMATCH) and upstream generation fault (H-UPSTREAM-GENERATION-FAULT) are SUPPORTED by E-01. Given this, the DEFINE gate returned CONDITIONAL_PASS, deferring three critical/high unknowns (U-LOC-UNKNOWN-CAUSE, U-EVENT-ORDER-CAUSE, U-LEGITIMATE-REJECT-SHARE) as open verification obligations outside release scope. The release decision is RELEASE_WITH_KNOWN_LIMITATION: what shipped is the diagnostic breakdown of reject reasons for DA-REJ (work item W-WI-DIAGNOSE-REJECT-REASONS, DONE), not an auto-fix/resubmit agent — the original requested solution was not built, because the evidence contradicted its premise and the root-cause questions needed to safely auto-fix remain unanswered.
key_points: Original request (CL-01/CL-02, from SH-REQ) was to deploy an AI agent to auto-fix and blindly resubmit rejected shipment notices, treating rejects as uniform/transient carrier flakiness.

Reject-log evidence E-01 (AUTHORITATIVE, COMPLETE for its sample) shows 3 sampled rejects split into 2 LOC_UNKNOWN and 1 EVENT_ORDER — two distinct reason categories, contradicting the 'flaky carrier' framing (E-02, NON_AUTHORITATIVE stakeholder opinion).

Handoff H-1 (ORG-A→ORG-B) is recorded HEALTHY and semantically VALID, supporting H-UPSTREAM-GENERATION-FAULT: the likely defect source is ORG-A's shipment-notice generation process P-1, not transmission or carrier instability.
Hypothesis H-AUTO-FIXABLE-ERRORS (simple correctable errors an agent could auto-fix) was REJECTED based on E-01/E-02; H-BUSINESS-RULE-MISMATCH and H-UPSTREAM-GENERATION-FAULT are SUPPORTED by E-01.

The DEFINE gate result was CONDITIONAL_PASS, deferring three unknowns (U-LOC-UNKNOWN-CAUSE, U-EVENT-ORDER-CAUSE, U-LEGITIMATE-REJECT-SHARE) as verification obligations (VOB-...) required BEFORE_RELEASE but placed outside this release's scope.
What was actually released/delivered is the reject-reason diagnostic breakdown for DA-REJ (work item W-WI-DIAGNOSE-REJECT-REASONS, status DONE) — not an auto-fix/resubmit agent.

Release decision is RELEASE_WITH_KNOWN_LIMITATION with no items on hold; three VOBs remain OPEN with their blocking scopes (investigate_upstream_generation_fault:P-1, investigate_business_rule_mismatch:ORG-B, classify_rejects_before_resubmission:DA-REJ) explicitly outside the released scope.
Metrics M-LOC-UNKNOWN-SHARE (0.667) and M-EVENT-ORDER-SHARE (0.333) are based on the 3-record sample; M-POST-FIX-REJECT-RATE has no current value yet (target <0.05).
limitations_explained: The reason-code distribution (2 LOC_UNKNOWN, 1 EVENT_ORDER) rests on only a 3-record sample and may not generalize to the full population of rejects.

The release does not resolve why LOC_UNKNOWN or EVENT_ORDER rejects occur: U-LOC-UNKNOWN-CAUSE and U-EVENT-ORDER-CAUSE remain OPEN/DEFERRED behind VOB-U-LOC-UNKNOWN-CAUSE and VOB-U-EVENT-ORDER-CAUSE respectively.

It is unknown what share of rejects are legitimate business decisions (e.g., duplicate/invalid shipments) rather than errors to fix — U-LEGITIMATE-REJECT-SHARE remains OPEN behind VOB-U-LEGITIMATE-REJECT-SHARE, which is CRITICAL impact.
Even expanding the sample size would only improve statistical confidence in the reason-code shares; it would not by itself diagnose the causal mechanism behind LOC_UNKNOWN or EVENT_ORDER.

The completeness of the DA-REJ data asset relative to the true full reject population is UNKNOWN (per unresolved sample-size question U-SAMPLE-SIZE-VALIDITY), so even a larger pull might not reflect the true full population.
No auto-fix or resubmission capability was built or released; success criteria SC-NO-BLIND-RESUBMIT and SC-REDUCE-REJECT-RATE are not yet validated, and M-POST-FIX-REJECT-RATE has no current value.
